sentences.text: Neutral Citation No. - 2024:AHC:6902 Court No. - 79 Case :- CRIMINAL APPEAL No. - 11300 of 2023 Appellant :- Rakesh Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Appellant :- Rajat Kumar Shukla
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Abhisht Jaiswal,Atharva Dixit Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Short Counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the respondent and rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the appellant today are taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned counsel for the respondent alongwith learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 02.11.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Mathura.

sentences.text: 1 It is submitted that in this case the victim who was major aged about 27 years at the time of alleged incident was a married lady.
Further submitted that there was dispute between him and her husband as a result the relations were developed between the victim and the present appellant.
There was conversation on mobile phone and physical relations were also developed between them with consent.

She went to various hotels where relations were established, thereafter, she started making pressure on the appellant to enter into marriage which he denied as a result present F.I.R.
was lodged with false allegations that on the pretext of false promise of marriage physical relations were established with her by administering intoxicant in juice.

Further submitted that the victim herself caused injury on her hand and got admitted in the hospital where she was treated and told the reason that she fell on the ground as was stated in the medical report prepared by the doctor.
It is also submitted that she mentioned in F.I.R. that such injury was caused by the appellant but it was totally false.

It is also submitted that there is no any material on record to show that she was made unclothed and her photographs were taken by the appellant and under threat to make them viral she was sexually exploited.
In this way, no case u/s 376 I.P.C. can be said to be made out against the appellant.
Entire allegations levelled in the F.I.R. and in the statement are false.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.
Appellant is in jail since 30.09.2023 having no criminal antecedent.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.

Learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and contended that in this case the appellant promised to marry with the victim as a result relations were established between both of them but later on he denied the marriage.
It is also contended that relations were established under the influence of intoxicants which was administered by the appellant himself.
In this way, he cannot be said to be innocent and offence u/s 376 I.P.C. is prima facie made out against him, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order dated 02.11.2023 suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant- Rakesh involved in Case Crime No.299 of 2023, under Sections 376, 328, 506,
323 I.P.C. and 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, Police Station Govind Nagar, District Mathura be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Rakesh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27861468/
2 the court concerned subject to following conditions.

sentences.text: Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
